title: Tenant-aware preemptive routing and hosted-fill safeguards
creator: Priya Shah
description: Problem: During strong surges some tenants experience long tail latency or request drops when their Dedicated pools saturate. Current behavior routes to Hosted as an uncontrolled failover which increases cost and can amplify noisy-tenant effects. We need a tenant-aware preemptive routing layer that: (1) minimizes user-visible SLO violations for high-priority tenants, (2) provides predictable cost/usage when Hosted is used to fill capacity, and (3) prevents cascading overload across tenants and regions.
acceptance_criteria: Configurable soft-reserve per-tenant (reserve percentage) implemented in routing decision that reduces sudden host fill usage under surge
Preemptive routing window (grace period) that allows short bursts to use Dedicated without immediate hosted-fill fallback
Hosted-fill rate cap per-tenant and per-region enforced (QPS and token budget) with circuit-breaker semantics
Model-variant demotion rules implemented: when Dedicated variant latency degrades, route to cheaper compatible variant on Hosted as controlled fallback
Metrics: per-tenant hosted-fill tokens, fallback count, average p95 latency before/after implemented and dashboards visible in Console
End-to-end e2e tests and canary rollout plan with automatic rollback on increased error rate or cost spike
implementation_notes: Routing decision will execute in two stages: soft-reserve check + hosted-fill budget check. Keep check fast (<200us) to not add tail latency.
Introduce tenant reservation table stored in orchestrator (epoched cache) and expose API to update reserves without restart.
Hosted-fill enforcement token bucket per-tenant in proxy with leaky-bucket refill based on tenant priority and monthly budget.
Variant demotion mapping maintained in model-catalog (compatible variant IDs). Demotion uses model-quality delta and cost delta thresholds.
Tunable knobs: reserve_pct, grace_window_ms, hosted_qps_cap, hosted_token_budget, demote_quality_threshold
Add tracing spans in router to correlate decision history (why: reserve hit / budget exceeded / variant demoted).
updates: 2026-03-01 - Created ticket after postmortem that identified noisy tenant causing 3% p99 regressions during peak.
2026-03-03 - Spike completed: validated soft-reserve logic in local simulator. Observed 40% reduction in immediate hosted usage for simulated bursts.
2026-03-05 - Design review with PM and SRE: agreed soft-reserve + hosted-token model. SRE requested per-region caps and emergency global circuit breaker.
2026-03-07 - Prototype of token-bucket enforcement merged to feature branch (PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/2987). Proxy integration in progress.
2026-03-09 - Integration tests failing intermittently when token buckets are reloaded; root cause: race on cache invalidation. Assigned to Alex to add epoching.
2026-03-10 - Added console dashboard spec and alert thresholds. QA plan drafted. Planning canary rollout across two low-risk regions first.
notes_on_tradeoffs: Strict hard-reserves guarantee tenant isolation but reduce overall utilization — we prefer soft-reserve with gradual enforcement to balance utilization and SLOs.
Adding more checks in the fast-path increases CPU; we constrained design to a two-check pipeline and micro-optimizations to avoid per-request DB lookups.
Model-variant demotion can introduce quality regressions; we only demote to verified compatible variants and add sampling to monitor output quality.
Per-tenant hosted caps risk starving background low-priority tenants; we will expose emergency uplift flow via Console for ops to approve temporary increases.
qa_plan: Unit tests for reserve logic and token-bucket enforcement
Synthetic load tests with mixed-tenant profiles (high-priority steady, low-priority bursty) in staging
A/B canary in two regions: measure p95/p99 latency, hosted token spend, error rate for 48h
Manual verification of console metrics and alert triggers
rollback_plan: Remote feature flag to disable tenant-aware preemption (toggle in orchestrator)
Automatic rollback triggers: >3x hosted cost delta or >1.5x error rate increase over baseline in canary
If soft-reserve toggled off, routing resumes previous behavior with immediate hosted fallback
